title: How much of Earth's water can we drink?

props.title: How much of Earth's water can we drink?
props.note: All the water on Earth = 100 squares

scenes.narration: Earth is covered in water. So how much of it can we actually drink?
Picture all of it as a hundred squares. About ninety-seven are salt water, in the oceans.
About two more are frozen in ice caps and glaciers. That leaves roughly one square.
And most of the fresh water isn't in rivers and lakes at all. It's frozen, or deep underground.

props.title: Every drop counts.
props.source: Figures rounded. Source: US Geological Survey

scenes.narration: So the water we can easily reach is precious. Every drop counts.
